title: Multiplicative Chow-Künneth decomposition and homology splitting of configuration spaces

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: A large embedded JPEG (“Figure 0”) depicts unrelated photographic/menu-like content and is inserted in the middle of the proof: “Then the result [image] computes \(H_c^*(F(X,n),\mathbb{Q})\) ...”. It has no mathematical content, caption, or connection to the stated construction, and breaks the sentence and proof. It appears to replace missing mathematical text or an intended diagram.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.10, assertion that the left vertical map is an isomorphism
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that \((R^1j'_* (V_a\boxtimes\mathbb Q))_\eta\) is one-dimensional and that “the left vertical map is an isomorphism.” But the source is the full group \(H^1(A_1\times A_1,V_a\boxtimes\mathbb Q)\cong H^1(M_{1,1},V_a)\). By the paper's own Section 3.3 formula, for even \(a>0\) this contains \(S_{a+2}\oplus\mathbb Q(-1-a)\). Whenever cusp forms of weight \(a+2\) exist (for example \(a=10\), where \(S_{12}\neq0\)), this source is not one-dimensional and cannot map isomorphically to a one-dimensional stalk. At most, the claim could concern the Eisenstein/Tate summand \(\mathbb Q(-1-a)\); as written, the claimed isomorphism and the ensuing proof are false.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.3 and Table 3, especially rows \(\lambda=(2)\) and \(\lambda=(1,1)\)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4.3 defines \(h_\lambda=\sum_i[H^i(H_{\infty,n},\mathbb Q)\otimes_{S_n}\sigma_\lambda]t^i\), so every coefficient must be the class of an actual mixed Hodge structure. Table 3 instead gives, for example, \(h_{(2)}=1-Lt+(L^2+L)t^2-\cdots\) and \(h_{(1,1)}=Lt^2-L^2t^3+\cdots\). In particular the coefficient of \(t\) in the first row is \(-L=-[\mathbb Q(-1)]\), which cannot be the class of any actual cohomology group. The same issue occurs for other negative coefficients in this table. The table could only represent an alternating/virtual invariant, but that is incompatible with the explicit definition of \(h_\lambda\) as a non-alternating sum of cohomology groups.

The reference list is materially incomplete relative to the citations in the text. For example, the paper cites [Voi14], [SV16], [FLV21b], [Cer83], [Tot96], [CL22], [Tav18], [Pet20], [Tub23], [Ivo16], [DJ20], [Wat18], [Pet13], [Pet15], [Pet16], [Sch95], [Tom24], and [PT14], but these entries are absent from the supplied bibliography, which ends at [PTY21]. These citations therefore cannot be checked and several substantive claims are left without identifiable references.
